source.title: Event-Grounded Sparse Autoencoders for Vision-Language-Action Policies
source.authors: Xin Jin; A. Chatterjee; Pranav Kumar; R. Paleja

page_placements.theme: Perturbation direction and baseline geometry matter

record.tranche_reason: The study does not analyze error predictability or scaling, but it replaces hidden states with SAE reconstructions and measures closed-loop success, testing whether omitting the SAE error affects behavior.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports closed-loop success under a reconstruction-only hook, which replaces the hidden state with its SAE reconstruction and therefore omits the residual error. These results bear on V5. The study does not compare this intervention with random errors of the same size or measure loss, and it does not analyze linear predictability, error norms across SAE sizes, token overlap, or error structure. Other interventions preserve the residual error; they do not compare keeping it against removing it.
record.test_reason: The study replaces VLA hidden states with their SAE reconstructions, dropping the error term, and measures closed-loop success against the unhooked policy. This bears on V5 (whether behaviour is lost when the error is not kept) in a new setting: robot VLA policies with BatchTopK SAEs. It has no matched-norm random-error comparison, no loss measure, and no analysis of error predictability, scaling or structure, so V1–V4 and V6 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the paraphrase overweights a secondary point. The main conclusion is that event-grounded SAE analysis is a practical, behaviour-anchored approach for VLA interpretability. It reveals architecture- and site-dependent effects: localized event-aligned effects in OpenVLA, weak single-feature leverage in the π0.5 backbone, and broad sensitivity in the action expert. SAE features form a sparse but imperfect causal basis. That offline FVE does not predict Hooked SR is a Section 4.1 finding, not the headline.
record.recipe_differences: Uses BatchTopK SAEs on VLA residual streams and measures closed-loop reconstruction fidelity; it does not perform the original study's analyses of SAE error predictability or scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction-hook effects vary strongly by architecture and intervention layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Decoder-vector steering at α=150 collapses OpenVLA SR to 0% versus 52% for a matched-norm random vector (Table 9). This concerns steering directions, not the SAE reconstruction error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE decoder directions are more behaviourally disruptive than matched-norm random directions in VLAs.

record.problems: The study does not compare omitted SAE error with random errors of matched size, and Hooked SR is a coarse behavioral measure rather than model loss. Reported Hooked SR is averaged across four suites, with 10 rollouts per task.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error from the input activation.
Error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, overlap of failing contexts, persistence with scale. Only one SAE size is trained per stream.
Whether reconstruction errors harm the model more than random errors of matched norm. Table 9's random-vector control concerns decoder-vector steering, not reconstruction error.
Split of the error into linear unlearned features and a nonlinear residual.
Circuit or steering analyses comparing results with and without the error term. Latent edits always preserve the error, and the error-dropped variant is never compared.
Whether dark matter shrinks with architecture or training changes. Only BatchTopK is used, and dead latents (3–8% alive in OpenVLA) are not linked to error effects.

missing.what: Hook-site comparison on OpenVLA LIBERO-Spatial layer 31. Reconstruction-only Hooked SR is 0.67 at resid_post and 0.83 at mlp_out, against a 0.80 no-intervention baseline. The error matters at resid_post but not at mlp_out.
missing.locator: Appendix L, 'Behavioral comparison of intervention hook sites', Figure 14

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3 because this is a new setting (robot VLAs, closed-loop success) rather than the original method. Hooked SR averages four suites with 10 rollouts per task, which is a coarse measure. The π0.5 SAEs are not overcomplete, which may explain their high fidelity. The authors attribute the OpenVLA collapse to discrete action tokens compounding small errors across closed-loop steps. That explanation concerns error size, not whether the error is pathological, so this study cannot separate V5 from simple sensitivity to perturbation size.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of the error vector is linearly predictable from the input activation.
Predictability of per-token error norms across SAE sizes, overlap of contexts where different sizes fail, and whether error persists with scale.
Whether reconstruction replacement harms model loss more than random errors of the same size; the study reports success rate, not this comparison.
Whether the linear component contains unlearned features and the nonlinear component resists dictionary learning.
The study tests effects on closed-loop success under reconstruction-only replacement, not the share of particular circuits or steering analyses that depends on retaining the error term.
Whether dark matter is mainly a training artifact or shrinks with improved architectures or end-to-end training.
